proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (Transpose), with the construction made explicit. ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch05.Submission, so the transpose is built from the standard basis.

1. Notation. For i in Fin n let e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n. These are the vectors of the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) R, so every v in R^n satisfies v = sum_i v_i e_i (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr), and <e_i, u> = u_i for every u in R^n (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left).

2. Definition of tau_0. For L in L(R^n, R^m) put tau_0(L) := sum_{i in Fin n} (innerSL R (L e_i)).smulRight e_i in L(R^m, R^n). Thus tau_0(L) w = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i. Each summand is a continuous linear functional w |-> <L e_i, w> times the fixed vector e_i, so tau_0(L) is a continuous linear map R^m -> R^n.

3. tau_0 is R-linear in L. For L, L' and every w: tau_0(L + L') w = sum_i <L e_i + L' e_i, w> e_i = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i + sum_i <L' e_i, w> e_i = tau_0(L) w + tau_0(L') w (additivity of the inner product in its first argument, add_smul, Finset.sum_add_distrib). For c in R: tau_0(c L) w = sum_i <c L e_i, w> e_i = sum_i (c <L e_i, w>) e_i = c tau_0(L) w (real_inner_smul_left, smul_smul, Finset.smul_sum). Hence tau_0 is a linear map L(R^n, R^m) -> L(R^m, R^n) (ext on w reduces both identities to the computations above).

4. Continuity. The space L(R^n, R^m) is finite-dimensional, so every linear map out of it into a normed space is continuous; LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap turns tau_0 into a continuous linear map tau with tau(L) = tau_0(L) for all L.

5. Adjoint identity. Fix L, w, v. By step 2, <tau(L) w, v> = <sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i, v> = sum_i <L e_i, w> <e_i, v> = sum_i <L e_i, w> v_i. On the other hand, by step 1 and linearity of L, L v = sum_i v_i L e_i, so <w, L v> = sum_i v_i <w, L e_i> = sum_i v_i <L e_i, w> (symmetry of the real inner product, real_inner_comm). The two sums agree term by term (commutativity of multiplication), so <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v>.

6. Hence tau is the required continuous linear map, which proves the existence statement.
key_steps: Define tau(L) w := sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i via innerSL/smulRight with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1
tau is linear in L (additivity and homogeneity of the inner product in its first slot)
tau is continuous because L(R^n, R^m) is finite-dimensional (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap)
Adjoint identity <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v> by expanding v = sum_i v_i e_i
